newsitem.title: USA: PacifiCorp seeks western U.S. grid operator.
newsitem.headline: PacifiCorp seeks western U.S. grid operator.

text.p: PacifiCorp on Wednesday called for the formation of an Independent System Operator for the Western U.S. power grid as a means for helping prevent further outages.
Both the July 2 and August 10 outages have raised concerns about the amount of power being transferred across the Western U.S.'s interconnected system.

PacifiCorp said the system is currently operated through voluntary cooperative agreements, but as competition grows it will become difficult to determine who has the responsibility and authority to coordinate operations.
The July outage began when two 345,000 volt transmission lines caused two of its power plant units in Wyoming to trip off line, a safeguard designed to protect remaining lines.

The problem was aggravated by several factors, such as problems with voltage support, high energy imports into the Northwest from Canada and high north-to-south power transfers from the Northwest to California, it said.
PacifiCorp said management of the system by an independent operator, regulated by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) could enhance reliability and move power more efficiently.
PacifiCorp added that it has led an effort among Northwestern investor-owned utlities to hand over the operation of their transmission systems to an independent operator.
This group, dubbed IndeGO, includes Idaho Power Co, Montana Power Co, PacifiCorp, Portland General Electric, Puget Sound Power and Light, Sierra Pacific Power Co, and Washington Water Power Co.
The group plans to file a proposal to FERC in December.
